claims.text: A CrMnFeCoNi-based HEA exposed to high-temperature air preferentially forms manganese-rich surface oxides.
High-temperature oxidation causes Mn depletion beneath the oxide scale through outward Mn diffusion.
The manganese-rich oxide scales formed by the untreated bond coat are non-protective.
Heating the bond coat at about 800°C under moderately low oxygen partial pressure will induce an alumina surface layer.
The pre-oxidation treatment will produce an alumina layer that is thin, continuous, dense, and adherent.
An alumina scale forms through outward diffusion of Al to the surface during oxidation or heating.
A continuous alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina scale retards outward Mn migration and preserves the composition of the underlying alloy.
Limiting oxygen ingress through the preformed alumina layer suppresses rapid Mn oxidation.
Suppressing Mn oxidation reduces both non-protective Mn-rich oxide formation and Mn depletion.
Reduced Mn depletion maintains sluggish diffusion and phase stability in the bond coat.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will develop thinner and more uniform oxide scales than untreated bond coats.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will exhibit less subsurface Mn depletion than untreated bond coats.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will have better high-temperature mechanical performance, durability, and reliability than untreated bond coats.
Untreated bond coats typically develop irregular manganese-rich scales and degrade faster under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The beneficial effect should persist from 800°C to 1100°C if the alumina layer remains intact during thermal cycling.
Temperatures above the proposed range or extreme thermal cycling may crack the alumina layer and compromise its benefit.
Alumina formation can be accompanied by Al depletion and phase transformation in the subsurface alloy.
